KY-2026-HJR81.policyArea: Budget And Financial Administration, Effective Dates, Emergency, Public Utilities
KY-2026-HJR81.aiSummary: This joint resolution would let the state budget director release part of the money already set aside for a water and wastewater aid program for troubled or low-income systems. It affects the Kentucky Water and Wastewater Assistance for Troubled or Economically Restrained Systems Program and the state agencies that manage those funds. It also declares an emergency, and it was signed by the governor as Acts Chapter 190.

KY-2026-SJR116.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the University of Kentucky, the University of Louisville, and Eastern Kentucky University to coordinate a search for actionable solutions to physician shortages and to explore and expand health care opportunities in medically underserved areas in collaboration with community, state agency, professional associations, and other stakeholders.
KY-2026-SJR116.summary: Direct the University of Kentucky, the University of Louisville, and Eastern Kentucky University to coordinate a search for actionable solutions to physician shortages and to explore and expand health care opportunities in medically underserved areas in collaboration with community, state agency, professional associations, and other stakeholders; require a report to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027; APPROPRIATION; EMERGENCY, EFFECTIVE July 1, 2026.

KY-2026-SJR116.aiSummary: The resolution directs the University of Kentucky, the University of Louisville, and Eastern Kentucky University to work together on ways to help with doctor shortages and improve health care in underserved areas. It also calls for them to work with local groups, state agencies, and professional groups, and to send a report to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027. It passed and became law, with an effective date of July 1, 2026.

KY-2026-SR112.title: A RESOLUTION encouraging the establishment of the Fatherhood and Family Engagement Task Force.
KY-2026-SR112.summary: Encourage the Legislative Research Commission to establish the Fatherhood and Family Engagement Task Force; recommend duties and membership of the task force; encourage the task force to meet at least monthly during the 2026 Interim of the General Assembly and submit a report to the Legislative Research Commission by December 1, 2026.
KY-2026-SR112.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)
KY-2026-SR112.policyArea: Children And Minors, Legislative Research Commission, Men
KY-2026-SR112.aiSummary: The resolution encourages the Legislative Research Commission to set up the Fatherhood and Family Engagement Task Force. It suggests what the task force should do and who should be on it. The task force would meet at least once a month during the 2026 interim and send a report by December 1, 2026.

KY-2026-SJR62.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Division of Water to provide recommendations and clear guidance on how local governments can more easily access jurisdictional streams and waterways for cleanup after a flood.
KY-2026-SJR62.summary: Direct the Energy and Environment Cabinet's Division of Water to prepare and submit a report to the Legislative Research Commission by December 15, 2026, on recommendations for state and local governments to more easily access public waterways after flooding for debris removal and clean-up.
KY-2026-SJR62.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SJR62.policyArea: Environment And Conservation, Flood Control And Flooding, Local Government
KY-2026-SJR62.aiSummary: The resolution would direct Kentucky’s Division of Water to prepare a report with ideas for state and local governments on how to get easier access to public streams and waterways after flooding. The report would focus on cleanup and debris removal after floods. It would be due to the Legislative Research Commission by December 15, 2026.

KY-2026-HCR103.title: A CONCURRENT RESOLUTION establishing the Health Care Workforce Task Force to identify strategies to increase the number of health care professionals while maintaining high quality standards of care.
KY-2026-HCR103.summary: Establish the Health Care Workforce Task Force to identify strategies to increase the number of health care providers while maintaining high quality standards of care; establish task force membership; require the task force to submit a report with recommendations to the Legislative Research Commission for referral to the Interim Joint Committees on Health Services and Education by December 1, 2026.
KY-2026-HCR103.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)
KY-2026-HCR103.policyArea: Education, Higher, Health Care Professionals, Legislative Research Commission
KY-2026-HCR103.aiSummary: The resolution would create a Health Care Workforce Task Force to look for ways to increase the number of health care workers while keeping care standards high. It would set who serves on the task force and require a report with recommendations to be sent by December 1, 2026. The measure affects health care workers, schools, and state lawmakers who review the report.

KY-2026-HB94.title: AN ACT relating to postsecondary education.
KY-2026-HB94.summary: Amend KRS 164.2951 to require the Council on Postsecondary Education to develop, implement, and maintain statewide transfer pathways available between the public postsecondary education institutions in selected baccalaureate programs; require the council to publish on its website a list of the available transfer pathways; require participating postsecondary education institutions to accept transfer credit, earned or accepted at the prior institution within pathways as general education or program-specific general education credit before applying credit as elective; require the council to provide written notification to public postsecondary education institutions and coordinate credit transfer discussions upon receiving notification of an institution seeking to make changes to curricula impacting lower-division courses.
KY-2026-HB94.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

actions.text: reported favorably, 1st reading, to Calendar with Committee Substitute (1)

KY-2026-HB94.policyArea: Education, Higher, State Agencies, Universities And Colleges
KY-2026-HB94.aiSummary: The bill would require Kentucky’s Council on Postsecondary Education to create and keep up statewide transfer paths for some bachelor’s degree programs at public colleges and universities. It would also require the council to post those paths on its website and would require schools in those paths to accept certain transfer credits as general education credit before treating them as elective credit. The council would also have to notify public colleges and help with credit transfer talks when a school plans changes that affect lower-level courses.

KY-2026-HB687.title: AN ACT relating to stray equines.
KY-2026-HB687.summary: Amend KRS 259.120 to allow the county judge/executive to contract for the performance of specific duties required to be performed when an equine is subject to being taken up by a person or organization that provides animal sheltering services; require the contract to be approved by the county fiscal court; establish immunity from criminal and civil liability.
KY-2026-HB687.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

actions.text: reported favorably, 1st reading, to Calendar with Committee Substitute (1)

KY-2026-HB687.policyArea: Agriculture, Animals, Livestock, And Poultry, County Judges/Executive
KY-2026-HB687.aiSummary: The bill would let a county judge/executive hire someone to do certain duties when a stray horse or other equine is taken up by an animal sheltering group. The county fiscal court would have to approve the contract. It would also give immunity from criminal and civil liability for those duties.

KY-2026-HB519.title: AN ACT relating to identity documents.
KY-2026-HB519.summary: Create a new section of KRS 186.400 to 186.640 to define "communication disorder"; establish that at the time of application for an instruction permit, operator's license, or personal identification card a person may choose to have a notation on the document indicating that they have a communication disorder; direct that no fee shall be charged for the inclusion or removal of a notation; provide that a person may request removal of the notation; direct that the Department of Kentucky State Police shall implement training on interacting with persons who have a communication disorder; amend KRS 186.531 to conform; EFFECTIVE July 1, 2027.
KY-2026-HB519.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB519.policyArea: Disabilities, Driver Licensing, Effective Dates, Delayed
KY-2026-HB519.aiSummary: The bill would let people ask for a note on an instruction permit, driver’s license, or state ID showing they have a communication disorder, which means trouble with speaking, understanding, or using words. It would also let them ask to remove that note later, with no fee for adding or removing it. The Kentucky State Police would have to train staff on how to interact with people who have a communication disorder. It would take effect July 1, 2027.
